scenes.tts: Why does a growth factor for nerve cells have a receptor named after a tumour?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Kinase from a Tumour. A neuron on one side, a colon tumour cell on the other.
scenes.narration: Why does a growth factor for nerve cells have a receptor named after a tumour?

scenes.tts: Start with the first neurotrophin receptor anyone cloned. It could not explain survival.
scenes.visual: A 1986 lab bench. A receptor shape labeled p75 with a question mark over the word survival.
scenes.narration: Start with the first neurotrophin receptor anyone cloned. It could not explain survival.

scenes.tts: In 1986, Moses Chao and colleagues transferred human D N A into mouse cells.
scenes.caption: In 1986, Moses Chao and colleagues transferred human DNA into mouse cells.
scenes.visual: Human DNA fragments enter a dish of mouse cells. On screen: Chao and colleagues, 1986.
scenes.narration: In 1986, Moses Chao and colleagues transferred human DNA into mouse cells.

scenes.tts: They found cells that made the human receptor, and cloned its gene.
scenes.visual: One cell lights up with receptor on its surface; its gene is pulled out.
scenes.narration: They found cells that made the human receptor, and cloned its gene.

scenes.tts: Eric Shooter's laboratory reported the rat receptor the next year.
scenes.visual: On screen: Shooter laboratory, rat receptor, 1987.
scenes.narration: Eric Shooter's laboratory reported the rat receptor the next year.

scenes.tts: This protein, p seventy five, bound N G F with low affinity. It had no kinase.
scenes.caption: This protein, p75, bound NGF with low affinity. It had no kinase.
scenes.visual: p75 binding NGF loosely; its inside is empty, with no kinase domain.
scenes.narration: This protein, p75, bound NGF with low affinity. It had no kinase.

scenes.tts: Neurons were known to have higher affinity sites as well.
scenes.visual: A neuron with two classes of NGF binding site, loose and tight, drawn without implying how many of each.
scenes.narration: Neurons were known to have higher affinity sites as well.

scenes.tts: On its own, p seventy five could not account for them.
scenes.caption: On its own, p75 could not account for them.
scenes.visual: The tight sites stay unexplained, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: On its own, p75 could not account for them.

scenes.tts: The kinase came from somewhere else entirely: a human colon tumour.
scenes.visual: Switch to the colon carcinoma cell.
scenes.narration: The kinase came from somewhere else entirely: a human colon tumour.

scenes.tts: In 1986, Mariano Barbacid's laboratory described an oncogene from that tumour.
scenes.visual: On screen: Martin-Zanca, Hughes and Barbacid, 1986.
scenes.narration: In 1986, Mariano Barbacid's laboratory described an oncogene from that tumour.

scenes.tts: Part of a tropomyosin gene had fused to the gene for a tyrosine kinase.
scenes.visual: Two gene blocks join: a tropomyosin block and a kinase block.
scenes.narration: Part of a tropomyosin gene had fused to the gene for a tyrosine kinase.

scenes.tts: The fusion kept the kinase on, without any ligand.
scenes.visual: The fused protein's kinase glows constantly, with no factor bound.
scenes.narration: The fusion kept the kinase on, without any ligand.

scenes.tts: The name comes from that fusion: tropomyosin receptor kinase.
scenes.visual: Letters T, R, K highlight in tropomyosin receptor kinase. On screen: trk.
scenes.narration: The name comes from that fusion: tropomyosin receptor kinase.

scenes.tts: The normal gene encoded a membrane receptor with no known ligand.
scenes.visual: The normal receptor in a membrane, its binding site empty, labeled orphan.
scenes.narration: The normal gene encoded a membrane receptor with no known ligand.

scenes.tts: If D C C from the netrin lesson comes to mind, it should.
scenes.caption: If DCC from the netrin lesson comes to mind, it should.
scenes.visual: A small DCC receptor icon appears beside it.
scenes.narration: If DCC from the netrin lesson comes to mind, it should.

scenes.tts: Here again, a gene first studied in cancer had a job in wiring the nervous system.
scenes.visual: Both icons tagged: found in cancer, works in neurons.
scenes.narration: Here again, a gene first studied in cancer had a job in wiring the nervous system.

scenes.tts: Now a test. Take a fibroblast that makes no Track receptor and ignores N G F.
scenes.caption: Now a test. Take a fibroblast that makes no Trk receptor and ignores NGF.
scenes.visual: A flat fibroblast in a dish. NGF added; nothing happens.
scenes.narration: Now a test. Take a fibroblast that makes no Trk receptor and ignores NGF.

scenes.tts: Give it the gene for the normal Track protein. Then add N G F. What should happen?
scenes.caption: Give it the gene for the normal Trk protein. Then add NGF. What should happen?
scenes.visual: Trk receptors appear on the fibroblast. NGF hovers above. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Give it the gene for the normal Trk protein. Then add NGF. What should happen?

scenes.tts: In spring 1991, two groups showed that N G F binds the Track protein and causes its tyrosine phosphorylation.
scenes.caption: In spring 1991, two groups showed that NGF binds the Trk protein and causes its tyrosine phosphorylation.
scenes.visual: NGF docks; phosphate tags appear on Trk. On screen: Kaplan and colleagues; Klein, Barbacid and colleagues, 1991.
scenes.narration: In spring 1991, two groups showed that NGF binds the Trk protein and causes its tyrosine phosphorylation.

scenes.tts: Barbacid's group also found that fibroblasts carrying Track divided in response to N G F, without needing p seventy five.
scenes.caption: Barbacid's group also found that fibroblasts carrying Trk divided in response to NGF, without needing p75.
scenes.visual: The fibroblast divides into two. No p75 on its surface.
scenes.narration: Barbacid's group also found that fibroblasts carrying Trk divided in response to NGF, without needing p75.

scenes.tts: The orphan kinase from a tumour was a receptor for N G F.
scenes.caption: The orphan kinase from a tumour was a receptor for NGF.
scenes.visual: The orphan label is replaced with: NGF receptor.
scenes.narration: The orphan kinase from a tumour was a receptor for NGF.

scenes.tts: Earlier, in Barbacid's laboratory, Ruediger Klein went looking for the Track gene in mouse brain.
scenes.caption: Earlier, in Barbacid's laboratory, Ruediger Klein went looking for the Trk gene in mouse brain.
scenes.visual: A library of clones; a probe searching. On screen: Klein, Barbacid laboratory.
scenes.narration: Earlier, in Barbacid's laboratory, Ruediger Klein went looking for the Trk gene in mouse brain.

scenes.tts: In his later account, he recovered a related gene instead. It was reported in 1989 as Track B.
scenes.caption: In his later account, he recovered a related gene instead. It was reported in 1989 as TrkB.
scenes.visual: A second, similar gene emerges, labeled trkB, 1989. Small note: Klein's later account.
scenes.narration: In his later account, he recovered a related gene instead. It was reported in 1989 as TrkB.

scenes.tts: A later search, with Fabienne Lamballe, found a third relative, Track C, reported in 1991.
scenes.caption: A later search, with Fabienne Lamballe, found a third relative, TrkC, reported in 1991.
scenes.visual: A third gene joins, labeled trkC. On screen: Lamballe, Klein and Barbacid, 1991.
scenes.narration: A later search, with Fabienne Lamballe, found a third relative, TrkC, reported in 1991.

scenes.tts: A search for one receptor had turned up a family of three.
scenes.visual: Three receptors side by side: TrkA, TrkB, TrkC.
scenes.narration: A search for one receptor had turned up a family of three.

scenes.tts: That is why the original Track protein is now called Track A.
scenes.caption: That is why the original Trk protein is now called TrkA.
scenes.visual: The first receptor's label updates to TrkA.
scenes.narration: That is why the original Trk protein is now called TrkA.

scenes.tts: One question stayed open. How p seventy five and Track A together give high affinity binding is still argued.
scenes.caption: One question stayed open. How p75 and TrkA together give high-affinity binding is still argued.
scenes.visual: p75 and TrkA side by side with a dotted line between them, labeled still argued.
scenes.narration: One question stayed open. How p75 and TrkA together give high-affinity binding is still argued.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: the survival receptor was found in cancer, and N G F turned it on.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: the survival receptor was found in cancer, and NGF turned it on.
scenes.visual: Takeaway on screen: the survival receptor was found in a tumour; NGF switches it on.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: the survival receptor was found in cancer, and NGF turned it on.
